title: Your AI assistant may push you pricier options if it thinks you're rich

beats: Same flight request. Two people. The AI shows the richer one pricier tickets.
Researchers at Cisco and Carnegie Mellon ran three hundred twenty-five thousand tests on thirteen AI models. Fake profiles. Real decisions: flights, health insurance, grad school.
Eight of the thirteen steered wealthier profiles toward pricier picks. It doesn't change the price. It changes which options you see.
The biggest gap? Claude Opus four point eight. A hundred ninety-eight dollars more on flights. Two hundred eighty-four more a month on health insurance.
Then researchers said: find the cheapest. Gemini two point five Flash still picked tickets two hundred eight dollars higher. GPT-5 and Claude shrank it to about twenty.
How does it know? Your emails. Two were enough, and it read the money ones first, ninety-seven percent of the time.
Hiding your job didn't help. It made one model's insurance gap forty percent bigger. Only hiding financial data worked.
Caveats: fake profiles, and it's a preprint. OpenAI says its shopping product differs. Anthropic and Google haven't commented.
So before you hand an AI your inbox: whose side is it on?
